title: Support multiple RPG rules packs
description: Design and implement rules-pack support for multiple tabletop RPG systems while preserving licensing boundaries, campaign compatibility, deterministic tool behavior, and system-specific terminology. A campaign binds to one base RPG rules system, such as D&D 5e SRD or Pathfinder 2e Remaster, plus an explicitly ordered stack of compatible additive packs such as expansions, bestiaries, or optional subsystems. The initial implementation must preserve existing SRD-backed behavior and add a real Pathfinder/ORC-backed fixture and broad level-1 Pathfinder character generation support.
design:
Goal: Support both distinct base RPG systems and additive expansion packs through a rules System Stack. Campaigns bind to exactly one base rules system plus an ordered list of compatible add-on packs. The binding distinguishes RPG type from expansion content, persists in the campaign SQLite database, and is used by lookup, module compatibility, tools, context assembly, and character creation.

Architecture: Add a `rules` subsystem beside the existing `srd` and `world` subsystems. Rules packs carry metadata for `systemId`, `packId`, `version`, role (`base` or `addon`), compatibility, dependencies, source, license/allowed-use policy, and explicit override declarations. The resolver validates the selected stack, sorts add-ons by explicit order, rejects incompatible systems or missing dependencies, and rejects duplicate record keys unless the later pack explicitly declares an override. Rules records expose provider-neutral fields: `systemId`, `kind`, `key`, `name`, structured `data`, `source`, `license`, and optional override metadata.

Campaign and module binding: Persist the resolved campaign rules binding in the campaign DB as authoritative campaign state using a singleton `campaign_rules_binding` table with base system/pack/version, ordered add-ons JSON, and resolution timestamp. The CLI registry may record pointer metadata, but play, checkpoint, restore, and unmanaged `LOREWEAVER_DB_PATH` campaigns read the DB binding. Module packs gain `rulesRequirements` declaring required base system/version and required/optional add-on packs. `createCampaign` validates the selected rules binding against module requirements before forking module content. Existing SRD-only campaign DBs without an explicit binding default/migrate to the current D&D SRD base binding.

Lookup and tools: Replace the model-facing `lookup_srd` seam with provider-neutral `lookup_rules`. The tool accepts `kind`, `name` or `ref`, and optional `systemId`; by default it resolves through the campaign binding. Tool results include the resolved record, source pack, license metadata, and override chain. `lookup_srd` may remain temporarily as a compatibility wrapper, but the default tool registry and system prompt should move to `lookup_rules` and avoid D&D-only language. Module encounter references move from `srdRef` to provider-neutral rules refs.

Character creation: Make character creation rules-system-aware. Existing D&D SRD character creation keeps current behavior through a D&D validator. Pathfinder gets a separate validator backed by Pathfinder rules records. The first deliverable favors broad, playable level-1 Pathfinder generation rather than a tiny fixture: ancestry, background, class, ability boosts, proficiencies, feats, equipment, spells where applicable, HP, and derived values. Data structures and validation seams should remain open to future advancement beyond level 1. The canonical `character` singleton remains the shared live-state projection for now, with system-specific sheet detail carried in JSON fields and the same `mutate_state` write path.

Licensing and storage: Rules-pack license metadata should reuse or generalize the existing `PackLicense` policy shape. Bundled/public rules packs must pass a shippable policy check; user-private packs can install under `<root>/rules-packs/` but are not bundled, published, or used for hosted/public demos without a later policy. Pathfinder material should use ORC-licensed rules content only and avoid Paizo reserved material/trademarks beyond permitted references; no Paizo compatibility logo/branding is needed for core fixtures. Bundled rules packs ship with core, non-bundled packs live under `<root>/rules-packs/`, and campaign DBs persist the binding rather than copying all rules data.

File map: Add `packages/core/src/rules/*` for pack types, validation, stack resolution, lookup, bundled D&D SRD adapter, Pathfinder fixture, and licensing policy. Update `packages/core/src/campaign.ts`, `packages/core/src/persistence/schema.ts`, `packages/core/src/world/types.ts`, `packages/core/src/world/validate.ts`, and `packages/core/src/world/forkCampaign.ts` for binding and module requirements. Update `packages/core/src/orchestrator/tools.ts` and `packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts` for `lookup_rules`. Update `packages/core/src/characterCreation.ts` or split into `packages/core/src/character/*` to dispatch by rules system. Update CLI campaign creation/play paths only where they need to select or pass the rules binding. Update docs in `docs/storage.md`, `docs/world.md`, and `docs/character-creation.md`.

Tradeoffs: The System Stack is more structured than a flat list but reflects the product model: one RPG type plus deterministic expansion order. It avoids full multi-engine duplication while allowing system-specific character validators where a single generic sheet would be premature. Explicit override declarations add authoring burden but prevent accidental shadowing and make lookup results auditable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rules-pack metadata validation covers system identity, pack identity, version, role, compatibility, dependencies, license policy, allowed use, and explicit overrides.
- At least two distinct base rules systems load in tests: existing D&D SRD behavior and a real Pathfinder 2e Remaster/ORC-backed fixture.
- Campaign DBs persist an authoritative rules binding with one base pack and ordered add-ons; existing SRD-only DBs without a binding continue as D&D SRD campaigns.
- Add-on ordering is deterministic; incompatible add-ons, missing dependencies, and duplicate record keys without explicit override declarations fail validation.
- Module packs declare rules requirements, and campaign creation rejects incompatible module/rules pairings before forking module content.
- Public/model-facing lookup uses `lookup_rules` and provider-neutral rule refs/results; default prompt/tool registry no longer assume only D&D SRD naming. Existing SRD lookup compatibility remains where needed during migration.
- Licensing/allowed-use metadata is enforced for bundled/public rules packs, including rejection of user-private or unshippable material at bundle/public boundaries.
- D&D SRD character creation behavior remains covered and passing.
- Pathfinder character creation validates a broad playable level-1 character draft, including ancestry, background, class, ability boosts, feats/proficiencies/equipment/spells as applicable, HP, and derived values, with structures open to later advancement.
- Tests cover pack validation, campaign binding persistence/defaulting, lookup routing, module compatibility, explicit override behavior, licensing rejection, D&D compatibility, and Pathfinder character validation.
- Final verification commands: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` pass.
close_reason: All 10 implementation tasks (x3w.9 – x3w.18) closed. Rules-pack support shipped: provider-neutral RulesPack metadata/validation/license; deterministic resolveRulesStack + lookupRulesRecord with overrides and add-on ordering; bundled DND5E_SRD_RULES_PACK (CC-BY-4.0) and PATHFINDER2E_REMASTER_RULES_PACK (ORC); campaign_rules_binding singleton table (schema v6→v7) with createCampaign default + legacy fallback; ModuleRulesRequirements + provider-neutral EncounterCreature.rulesRef; lookup_rules tool replacing lookup_srd in the default registry and system prompt; system-aware completeCharacterCreation dispatcher with the existing D&D path preserved and a broad level-1 Pathfinder validator; CLI flows persist the default D&D binding end-to-end; storage/world/character-creation docs and README updated. Final: npm run typecheck and npm run test pass (388 passed, 2 documented skips, 50 files).
